source: STEER Project (Save the Children, iDE Cambodia, and the Cambodian Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries) - "Guide on Banana Cultivation Techniques" (សៀវភៅណែនាំស្តីអំពី បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក), February 2020
text:
The guide closes with a simple seasonal planning table linking banana's production cycle to market demand: planting is best timed so that harvest (roughly 9-12 months later) lands when fresh fruit and processed banana products are in steady demand, and the source flags certain months as higher-demand periods for banana in general based on typical consumption patterns.

Farmers are encouraged to plan planting dates with this demand calendar in mind, since timing bunches to mature ahead of higher-demand periods can improve the price received, in the same way market gardeners plan vegetable planting around expected demand peaks.
